general_information.Description: This course will explore existing modern typographical ideas and techniques and attempt to expand on students’ typographical range. Students will investigate the communication of content and the emotional qualities of text. Students will further develop their visual and conceptual fluency and create integrated communication design solutions. Emphasis will be placed on using typography, aesthetics, and composition to construct meaningful imagery and effectively solve communication problems. This course uses the art of typography, aesthetic element,..., to build up ideas and apply them in designing products for graphic design such as: publication, branding systems.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfil tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose. Computer have to installed some version of design software such as Photoshop, Illustrator for design assignments, and Powerpoint for presentations. - Read the textbook in advance

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze and Apply Typographic Principles and Conventions: Understand and apply established typographic terminology, layout grids, alignment techniques and structural systems.
Employ Typography for Visual Hierarchy and Communication: Apply principles of hierarchy and dominance to create impactful typographic layouts that effectively convey meaning.
Develop Typographic Fluency and Best Practices: Demonstrate proficiency in typographic design, incorporating best practices for legibility and aesthetic impact.
Develop a Critical Eye for Typography: Analyze the historical and theoretical context of typography, and evaluate its role in design.
Evaluate and Refine Own Typographic Work: Critically assess own typographic designs and identify areas for improvement.

assessments.Grading Guide: - Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. - Teacher give marks on student's student's Class participation and preparation only after the Portfolio submission.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Group Present- Each group works on researching some specific products that will be used for Practice 1 and 2, such as book layout, magazine layout, brochure/leaflet/website layout, etc.- Research existing examples of the chosen layout type to identify best practices and potential weaknesses. Students deliver a slide presentation with full documentation of the research process (AI Use Log ) and present a counter-argument in Q&A.
assessments.Grading Guide: The evaluation will consider the following criteria: Research plan & sources (20%). Analysis & findings (20%). Core making / prototyping (30%), Integration & iteration (20%), Slides & presentation (story + Q&A) (10%). Students deliver a slide presentation with full documentation of the research process (AI Use Log) and present a counter-argument in Q&A.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: - Understand the fuction of different sections of a book. - Identify and explain the role of non-text elements (notes, captions, sidebars, etc).- Recognize the importance of font choices for both body text and display elements (heading, titles). - Learn basic principles of combining typefaces effectively.- Understand how to design visually appealing and functional page layouts and spreads.- Consider principles of hierarchy, balance, legibility and readability.- Gain a basic awareness of design consideration specific to books intended for printing.
assessments.Grading Guide: The evaluation will consider the following criteria: Brief & content plan (10%), Type system, grid & styles (20%), Core making / prototyping (30%), Integration, testing & iteration (20%), Final delivery & documentation (20%).

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Magazine/Brochure/Booklet design- Understand the common structural elements, design principles, and audience considerations of different layouts (magazine, brochure, leaflet, etc).- Learn how to effectively guide the reader's eye through the layout using elements like typography, color, image placement, etc.

schedule.Topic: Practice 1 Designing a Book Research + Individual Presentation
schedule.Student's Tasks: - Students can start with the simplest books: novels, memoirs, essays, and narrative nonfiction.Students are not allowed to choose a self-help book. - Students research all the details inside and out of the book, then give the lecturer a short individual presentation. - Time: 5-10 minutes per student 'INDIVIDUAL WORK - Book construction: Each part of the book has its role to play and its assigned place in the whole. - Cover design basics - Fonts for text: There’s no bigger decision a designer makes than selecting the fonts that will be used for the book’s text. - Fonts for display: Knowing how to choose and combine typefaces is critical for the designer. - Architecture of the book page: Building pages and spreads is at the heart of book design. - Non-text book elements: Every book incorporates elements that are outside the text itself, like notes, bibliographies, part- and chapter-opening pages, captions, sidebars, pull-quotes, and others. Each has to blend well with the rest of the book, and stand out when necessary. - Minimum of 45 pages that included text.
